native_result.query: What proportion of studies in Experimental Economics were conducted in a lab setting?
native_result.HypoA: In Experimental Economics, all studies (both original and replication) were conducted in a lab setting (100%), while in Psychology, a small proportion of replication studies were also conducted online (8.8%)
native_result.HypoB: Among the 18 Experimental Economics originals in the supplied meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv (project=='ee', deduped by id), all 18 were conducted in a lab setting under the in-person operationalization (online.o == 0): 18/18 = 100.00%. Sensitivity range across alternative operationalizations is 94.44%–100.00% (17/18 under the strict students-only reading vs. 18/18 under in-person-only, in-person + subject pool ∈ {students, community}, in-person + compensation ∈ {cash, mixed}, and original-and-replication-both-in-person). The single row responsible for the S1↔S2 discrepancy is Charness & Dufwenberg (AER 2011) "Participation", whose subject pool is labelled "community" but whose experiment was clearly in-person. The replication side mirrors the original side exactly (online.r == 0 and same_online == 1 for all 18 rows), so the proportion is identical whether originals or replications are counted. CSV2 carries no lab/setting fields and contributes only cross-confirmation of the 18 ee studies by first-author surname (18/18 match). Caveat: n = 18 is the entirety of the ee subset in this dataset, not a population estimate.
native_result.WorkflowB: Load CSV1 (927 × 57); filter to project=='ee' (n=18); dedupe by id (defensive, no-op since 18/18 unique). Compute primary proportion as count(online.o==0) / count(project=='ee') = 18/18. Run five sensitivity checks S1–S5 on the same 18 rows. Cross-confirm the 18 originals against CSV2 (which has 18 'Experimental Economics' rows but no setting columns) by surname-set equality. Persist results to artifacts/results.json and print a summary.
